title: Automated synthetic-tenant safety net and dynamic burst governor
creator: Priya Shah
description: Summary: During a capacity event on 2026-03-02 a single tenant generated sustained high token throughput combined with heavy KV-cache churn which caused eviction storms and p99 tail latency spikes across a Dedicated GPU pool. Symptoms included large scheduling queues, elevated retry rates for medium-priority tenants, and burst tokens being consumed in short windows that starved neighbors. Impact: several enterprise customers experienced degraded latency for 30-90 minutes; automated failover to a smaller model variant occurred for a subset but some routes saw elevated error rates. Root causes: 1) reservation under-provisioning for a tenant whose workload suddenly grew (mis-sized reservation assumptions based on 30d average); 2) lack of an automated noisy-tenant detector that correlates KV cache churn and token-rate anomalies; 3) the existing burst policy allowed high instantaneous token bursts without decay penalties leading to short-term neighbor starvation. Goal: implement a short+medium+long roadmap to contain noisy tenants quickly, prevent reservation drift, and replace the static burst tokenbucket with a dynamic burst governor that enforces burst budgets, decay, and progressively stronger soft-fencing for repeat offenders. Success criteria: - No dedicated-pool p99 latency degradation caused by a single tenant in synthetic tests (50-run stress series) - Reduction in customer-impacting incidents for Dedicated pools by 80% in the next quarter - New telemetry and alerts for noisy-tenant signals with <5 minute detection time and actionable runbook entries
action_items: Short-term (1-2 weeks): emergency soft-fence runbook + circuit breaker: implement tenant soft-fence API (owner: Ethan Cole, estimate: 2) - allows ops to throttle token-rate and temporarily bump reservation via admin call
Short-term: apply conservative burst cap rollout to all Dedicated pools (owner: SRE team - Lia Chen, estimate: 1) - reduces max instantaneous tokens per tenant by 30% behind feature flag

Medium-term (2-6 weeks): noisy-tenant detector service (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 5) - stream KV cache churn, token-rate, goroutine scheduling latency into an anomaly classifier and surface tenant fingerprints to console and alerts

Medium-term: dynamic reservation recalibrator (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 8) - background service that proposes reservation adjustments based on p95 token/sec, historical variance, and recent canary signals; offers dry-run and automatic apply modes

Medium-term: burst governor replacement (owner: Ethan Cole, estimate: 8) - tokenbucket -> decay-based burst budget with progressive penalties (penalty window, budget decay rate, soft-quarantine) and tenant penalty scoring
Telemetry and testing (parallel): synthetic-tenant generator added to CI (owner: QA - Lina Patel, estimate: 3) - create multi-tenant stress tests that exercise KV churn and random spike patterns

Observability: new dashboards and SLIs (owner: Observability - Noah Park, estimate: 3) - KV churn rate, tenant token-rate heatmap, burst budget consumption, per-tenant p99 latency, automated incident pulse charts
Runbook and docs: update Dedicated Playbook + run automated drills (owner: Solutions - Maya Thompson, estimate: 2)
